summary: Say the counting numbers in order by ones, from 1 all the way to 20.
Say which number comes just before or just after another number from 1 to 10.
Count a group of up to 10 objects and start to match it with the written number.
Look at a written number from 0 to 10 and say its name.
Count up to 10 objects, touching or saying one number for each object.
Count up to 10 objects and know the last number said tells how many there are.
Count two groups of up to 10 objects each to find out which group has more.
Show adding and taking away within 5 using objects, fingers, moving around or simple drawings.
With help, solve adding and taking-away stories told by the teacher, using up to 5 objects.
Split a group of up to 5 objects into two parts, like 2 blue and 3 yellow.
Use objects to find two amounts that make 5 together, like 2 and 3 or 0 and 5.
Copy, continue and make up simple repeating patterns, like red, blue, red, blue.
Describe things with words like long or short, heavy or light, big or small, near or far.
Put two things side by side to tell which is longer, heavier or bigger.
Sort objects into groups by a given feature, like color, size or shape.
Count each sorted group and tell which group has more, which has less, or if they are the same.
Name the shapes of things nearby and say where they are: above, below, beside, in front, behind.
Name basic shapes whether they are big or small, turned or flipped.
Start to notice that some shapes are flat and others are solid.
Talk about a flat shape's size and how many sides and corners it has.
Make basic shapes with blocks, stickers, play dough or art supplies.
Try putting shapes together to make new ones, like two triangles making a bigger shape.
